channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: UAE Presidential Adviser Gargash says more realistic approach needed beyond MoU
item.description: United Arab Emirates (UAE) Presidential Adviser Anwar Gargash said during the European trading session on Monday that political solutions must begin with de-escalation and restoring normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key passage to almost one-fifth of global energy supply.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Hesitates near 0.8550 with the risk-off mood capping rallies
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is looking for direction against the British Pound (GBP) on Monday, following a sharp reversal last Friday, with bears eyeing the bottom of the last two weeks’ trading range, just below 0.8550.

item.title: Gold keeps the red below $4,450 as Fed hike bets offset soft USD amid Iran tensions
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to capitalize on a modest intraday bounce from sub-$4,400 levels – a one-and-a-half-week low – and sticks to a negative bias heading into the European session on Monday.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Growth supports INR against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank strategists highlight resilient domestic growth, supported by strong industrial production and investment activity ahead of the Q2 GDP release. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) expects growth to moderate to 6.7% in FY2026-27 while inflation remains contained at 5.0%.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gathers strength above 0.5900 on stronger China PMI data
item.description: The NZD/USD pair gains momentum to near 0.5915 during the early European trading hours on Monday. Better-than-expected Chinese economic data provides some support to the China-proxy New Zealand Dollar (NZD) against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Indian Rupee ticks lower as renewed Middle East tensions lift oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens slightly lower against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week. The USD/INR pair ticks up to near 95.43, as higher oil prices due to renewed tensions between the United States (US) and Iran have weighed on the Indian currency.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Market needs more than BoJ pricing – OCBC
item.description: OCBC FX Strategist Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the Japanese Yen (JPY) has already benefited from aggressive market pricing for Bank of Japan (BoJ) tightening, with an 85% chance of a September hike implied.

item.title: Asian stock markets face slight pressure from renewed geopolitical risks, hawkish Fed bets
item.description: Asian equity markets remain under pressure at the start of the week, as risk sentiment turns sour due to renewed tensions in the Middle East and a sharp increase in Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike expectations.

item.title: Brent: Hormuz tensions keep prices supported above $90 - ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that oil prices, including ICE Brent, started the week stronger after US strikes on Iran raised concerns over Persian Gulf supply.

item.title: British Pound: Downside risks with 1.3480 in sight against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that GBP/USD fell sharply to 1.3527 and closed at 1.3540, contradicting expectations for range trading. Intraday, they see limited further losses within 1.3520–1.3570 due to oversold conditions.

item.title: British Pound holds losses amid geopolitical tensions, Fed tightening hopes
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) edges up on Monday but remains close to two-week lows against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro: Warsh speech weighs on EUR against US Dollar – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team notes that Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushed EUR/USD lower, with markets now pricing September as nearly a coin-flip for a rate hike.

item.title: Euro falls against Japanese Yen ahead of German inflation data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is down 0.1% to near 185.20 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Monday. The cross faces pressure as the Japanese Yen (JPY) outperforms its peers amid fears that the Bak of Japan (BoJ) will raise interest rates in the September policy meeting.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Gains ground to near 1.1600, bullish vibe prevails above 100-day SMA
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades in positive territory around 1.1590 during the early European trading hours on Monday. However, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited as traders ramped up bets on a rate hike after hawkish remarks by Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Retreats from one-month top as bullish bias remains below 160.00
item.description: The USD/JPY pair retreats from the 160.20 area, or a one-month high retested earlier this Monday, and, for now, seems to have snapped a five-day winning streak. Spot prices slide to the 159.80-159.75 region during the Asian session, though the downside potential seems limited.

item.title: Iran’s IRGC claims it shot down US drone, attacked UAE air base
item.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz using air defense missiles, causing it to crash into Gulf waters, Mehr news agency reported on Monday.

item.title: WTI rises to near $84.50 as IRGC claims supertanker struck by mines in Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rebounds and continues its intraday gains, trading around $84.40 per barrel during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Holds above 0.7150 on soft USD; Fed/Iran risks curb upside
item.description: The AUD/USD pair attracts some buyers in the vicinity of mid-0.7100s at the start of a new week, stalling Friday's retracement slide from its highest level since mid-May. Spot prices, however, lack bullish conviction and remain below the 0.7200 mark through the Asian session.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Declines to near 114.50, but maintains bullish tone above 100-day SMA
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in negative territory around 114.50 during the early European session on Monday.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains as US Dollar weakens despite Fed Chair Warsh’s hawkish remarks
item.description: USD/CHF holds losses after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around 0.8090 during the Asian hours on Monday. The currency pair edges lower as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following comments from Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius.

item.title: United States Dollar Index trades slightly lower at the start of the US NFP week
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is slightly down in the Asian trading session at the start of the week. The US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenback’s value against its peers, corrects 0.1% to near 99.58 after a strong Friday.

item.title: United States: Labour market watch – NBC Economics and Strategy
item.description: NBC Economics and Strategy report that U.S. nominal personal income rose 0.4% in July, double expectations, while spending increased 0.2% and real disposable income climbed 0.4% with flat real spending.

item.title: United States Dollar: Rebound needs stronger payrolls data – TD Cowen
item.description: TD Cowen’s Washington Strategy team, led by Chris Krueger, notes that a durable rebound in the Dollar hinges on stronger US policy follow-through and renewed upside surprises in US data.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $66.00 amid Fed Chair Warsh’s hawkish tone
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around $66.10 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Monday. The non-yielding Silver declined following hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh.

item.title: Australian Dollar eases from July 9 high vs New Zealand Dollar; awaits Aussie GDP and RBNZ
item.description: The AUD/NZD cross turns positive for the fourth straight day following an intraday fall to the 1.2065 area and climbs to a fresh high since July 9 during the Asian session on Monday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar strengthens despite hawkish Fed rhetoric
item.description: The USD/CAD pair edges lower to around 1.3890 during the Asian trading hours on Monday. Renewed tensions between the US and Iran boost crude oil prices, supporting the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: British Pound bounces off over one-week low vs soft USD; upside potential seems limited
item.description: The GBP/USD pair edges higher at the start of a new week, reversing a part of Friday's heavy losses to over a one-week trough.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar inches higher as China’s Manufacturing PMI ticks up in August
item.description: NZD/USD remains subdued for the second successive day, trading around 0.5910 during the Asian hours on Monday. However, the NZD/USD pair pares some of its daily losses as the New Zealand Dollar receives minor support following the release of China's NBS Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data.

item.title: Gold drifts lower below $4,450 as hawkish Warsh remarks lift Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) attracts some sellers to near $4,445 during the early Asian trading hours on Monday. The precious metal edges lower on a surprisingly hawkish speech by Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole economic symposium.
